content.value_statement: Presentation workflows often need reliable ODP, PPTX, and PDF handling across tools. This skill guides LibreOffice Impress creation, conversion, and automation workflows for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Create ODP presentations from scratch or from reusable templates.
Convert presentations among ODP, PPTX, PDF, HTML, and SWF where LibreOffice supports the route.
Guide batch conversion workflows with LibreOffice command-line tools.
Describe Python UNO automation for slide creation and document control.
Support template-based content replacement inside ODP files.
Help plan slide masters, layouts, notes, shapes, images, and charts.
limitations: Requires LibreOffice and related command-line tools to be installed.
Conversion results can vary by fonts, media, and LibreOffice version.
Does not replace manual review of visual layout and slide timing.
UNO automation examples require a running LibreOffice listener for socket workflows.

use_cases.title: Automate Team Reports
use_cases.description: Create recurring ODP or PDF decks from templates and updated business data.

use_cases.title: Convert Client Deliverables
use_cases.description: Convert existing ODP or PPTX decks into PDF exports for review and distribution.

use_cases.title: Build Presentation Pipelines
use_cases.description: Use LibreOffice command-line and UNO workflows inside repeatable document generation systems.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the impress skill to outline a five-slide ODP presentation about [topic]. Include titles, body text, and speaker notes.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Presentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the impress skill to convert [file] from ODP to PDF. Include the LibreOffice command and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Slides From a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the impress skill to design a template workflow for [template.odp] using data fields [fields]. Include file handling steps and review checks.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Batch Conversion With UNO
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the impress skill to plan an automated pipeline that creates, updates, and exports multiple presentation files using LibreOffice UNO.

output_examples.input: Create a quarterly business review deck from a standard ODP template.
output_examples.output: A slide plan with section titles, template placeholders, speaker notes, and a checklist for generating the final ODP and PDF files.

output_examples.input: Convert a folder of ODP decks to PDF for stakeholder review.
output_examples.output: A batch conversion workflow, required LibreOffice setup checks, expected output naming, and visual validation steps.

output_examples.input: Plan a Python UNO workflow for image and chart slides.
output_examples.output: An automation plan that covers LibreOffice listener setup, slide creation, content insertion, saving, and cleanup.

best_practices: Keep source ODP files and templates under version control.
Validate exported PPTX and PDF files visually before distribution.
Use slide masters and embedded fonts for consistent output.
anti_patterns: Do not run conversion commands on untrusted files without isolation.
Do not assume PPTX exports preserve every animation or layout detail.
Do not overwrite source decks before reviewing generated outputs.

faq.question: Does this skill require LibreOffice?
faq.answer: Yes. Command-line conversion and UNO automation require LibreOffice installed in the target environment.

faq.question: Can it create PPTX files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide ODP to PPTX export when LibreOffice supports the source deck.

faq.question: Can it edit existing decks?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides workflows for template updates, content insertion, and format conversion.

faq.question: Does it guarantee identical formatting?
faq.answer: No. Fonts, media, transitions, and converter versions can affect visual results.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it in automation?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes shell and Python workflows they can adapt after user approval.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive presentations?
faq.answer: Use local files and trusted templates. Review outputs before sharing confidential content.
